title: Certificates of Deposit: reversing a grace-period withdrawal penalty in full, once
content:
## Scope

This rule decides, for a Certificates of Deposit penalty charged on money taken out during the grace period, whether it is reversed and for how much.

## Rule

1. **In full.** A penalty charged on a grace withdrawal that was the owner's own is reversed with the adjustment reason bank error, in full and never in part.
2. **Amount.** The reversal amount is the booked penalty amount to the cent, with no further rounding.
3. **Once only.** A penalty that already has a penalty reversal entry pointing to it is not reversed again.
4. **Not taken in grace.** When the withdrawal was not taken during the grace period, nothing is written under these rules.

## Truth table

| Withdrawal taken during grace | Owner's own withdrawal | Already reversed | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | No | Reverse the whole booked penalty |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Not reversed again |
| Yes | No | Any | Not reversed under these rules; handled as a disputed transaction |
| No | Any | Any | Nothing written under these rules |

## Cases (hypothetical penalties)

| Booked penalty | Situation | Amount reversed |
|---|---|---|
| 88.46 | Taken in grace, owner's own, never reversed | 88.46 |
| 88.46 | Same, but a reversal entry already points to it | None |
| 12.07 | Not taken in grace | None under these rules |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

| Wrong reading | Correct basis |
|---|---|
| Only the part of the penalty above what an early withdrawal would have cost is credited. | The penalty is reversed in full, never in part. |
| The amount is recalculated and rounded before crediting. | The booked amount is credited to the cent with no further rounding. |
